There's a holdover from dogtraining I try to remind myself of: Personality is largely an illusion. People are hugely associative learners too and unwittingly and unknowingly learn lots of (often very pointless) habits and associations early in life. Just because someone asks the same dumb question 5 times doesn't mean they're dumb or lazy - it means someone taught them a dumb strategy about school, or they're avoidant about it (usually because of negative associations) or any other number of things.

Intelligence, in as far as it is demonstrable, is almost entirely behavioral. That is the student that knows how to find reinforcement doing math will do well no matter what - bridging large gaps of knowledge and skill with practice and time. The student who has been taught largely by rote and knows various rote strategies and really just doesn't get that tiny kick of dopamine - they'll still feel a little bit like math idiots, even after they have degrees.
